texts.facts: The present accident claim is based on a detailed accident report (Dar) filed by the police in terms of provisions of Mv Act. Nafiz (Dar) vs Pawan Kumar (231/19Ppp) on 14 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124129897/ 1 2. The brief facts of the case are that on 19.11.2019, vide GD no.027A dated 19.11.2019, information regarding accident was received. Ct. Suresh reached at the spot and came to know that injured had already been removed to hospital. On reaching hospital, it was found that injured was unfit for statement. On 21.11.2019, statement of injured was recorded. He told that on 19.11.2019 at around 11 pm, he parked his truck at ICD Depot and was going towards Dhaba for having dinner. At that time, one truck bearing no.RJ-09GA-8957(hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle) came at high speed and hit him. Due to the impact, he fell down and sustained injuries. His brother in law took him to AIIMS trauma center. 3. An FIR no.231/19 dated 21.11.2019 was registered u/s 279,337 of IPC at PS Pul Prahladpur and the matter was investigated. After investigation a charge sheet u/s 279/338 IPC was filed before concerned criminal court against the driver of the offending vehicle while a DAR was filed before this Tribunal. 4. Respondent no.1 is driver, Respondent no.2 is the owner of offending vehicle and Respondent no.3 is the insurance company with which the offending vehicle was insured. 5. In response to the DAR, a legal offer was filed on behalf of Digitally signed CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.07.14 17:21:02 +0530 MACT NO:206/20 Nafiz v. Pawan Kumar P.No. 2 Of 17 BK insurance company. No reply was filed by Respondent no.1 and 2 despite opportunity. 6. After completion of pleadings, following issues were framed on 21.10.2021. 1. Whether the injured suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 19.11.2019 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no.RJ-09GA-8957 being driven by R-1, owned by R-2 and insured by R-3?OPP. OPP. 3. Relief. 7. To prove his claim, petitioner led his evidence by examining himself as PW-1 by way of affidavit as Ex.PW-1/A. In his evidence, he reiterated the fact as stated in the DAR. He deposed that he sustained fracture in waist and upper legs and injuries on other body parts. He was taken to AIIMS hospital where he was treated. At the time of accident, he was working as driver at ICDD deport, Tughlakabad and earning Rs.30,000/-p.m. He relied upon copy of FIR as Ex.PW-1/A, DAR as Ex.PW-1/B, Medical treatment and bills as Ex.PW-1/C and blood bank receipt as Ex.PW-1/D. He was duly cross - examined by learned counsel for insurance company. Nafiz (Dar) vs Pawan Kumar (231/19Ppp) on 14 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124129897/ 2 No evidence was led by Respondents. 8. Final arguments in details were addressed on behalf of the claimant/injured and the insurance company. Before proceeding to decide the above issue, it is apposite to note that as a settled principle of law, proceedings under The Motor Vehicle Act are not considered akin to the proceedings in a civil suit and hence strict rules of evidence are not applicable. Reliance is placed upon decision in Bimla Devi & ors. vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors. (2009) 13 SC 535, in Parmeshwari vs. Amir Chand & Ors., 2011 (1) SCR 1096 and National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ 287, wherein it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view has to be taken. 10. In the instant case, petitioner Nafiz Ahmad has testified the date as well as the manner of accident. He has specifically stated that the offending vehicle hit him while he was crossing the parking. He also stated that the offending vehicle drove to its right and then to its left (i.e. in a zig zag manner) before hitting the petitioner. Though suggestions have been put to suggest the negligence on the part of the petitioner, no cogent proof has been brought on record by the insurance company to prove contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner. Further, learned counsel for insurance company has pleaded a delay of two days in lodging of the FIR as a ground to doubt the veracity of petitioner's claim. It is, however, seen that an MLC was Digitally signed CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.07.14 17:21:19 +0530 MACT NO:206/20 Nafiz v. Pawan Kumar P.No. 4 Of 17 BK prepared on the same date of the accident i.e. 20.11.2019. Medical documents and discharge summary also reveals that the petitioner remained admitted in AIIMS hospital from 20.11.2019 to 27.11.2019. During this time, petitioner also underwent surgery. 11. Further, after investigation, the police has filed a chargesheet against Respondent no.1.
texts.arguments: In National Insurance Co. vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of charge sheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. To rebut the claim of the petitioner, none of the respondents Nafiz (Dar) vs Pawan Kumar (231/19Ppp) on 14 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124129897/ 3 have not led any evidence in defence. It may further be noted that in Cholamandlam insurance company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. As regards the quantum of compensation, this court is governed by the law laid down by Hon'le Supreme Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343, Sarla Verma & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Ors. (2003) 6SCC 121 and National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi & Ors.(2017) 16 SCC 680. The gist of the law is that the object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. 24.
